text: Then, this very morning. <break time="0.8s" /> Mister Wilson went to work as usual. <break time="0.8s" /> And found the office door. <break time="0.8s" /> Shut and locked. <break time="0.8s" /> In the middle of the door. <break time="0.8s" /> Was a small card. <break time="0.8s" /> That said. <break time="0.8s" /> The Red Headed League is dissolved. <break time="0.8s" /> October 9, 1890. <break time="0.8s" /> Holmes and I looked at the card. <break time="0.8s" /> And at the sad face behind it. <break time="0.8s" /> And we both. <break time="0.8s" /> Burst out laughing. <break time="0.8s" /> Wilson asked the landlord. <break time="0.8s" /> Who said that he had never heard of the League. <break time="0.8s" /> Or of anyone called Duncan Ross. <break time="0.8s" /> The red headed man in that office. <break time="0.8s" /> He said. <break time="0.8s" /> Was a lawyer named William Morris. <break time="0.8s" /> Who had moved out the day before. <break time="0.8s" /> Wilson went to the new address. <break time="0.8s" /> But he found that it was a factory. <break time="0.8s" /> That made artificial kneecaps. <break time="0.8s" /> Holmes then asked whether. <break time="0.8s" /> The assistant was a small, quick man. <break time="0.8s" /> With no hair on his face. <break time="0.8s" /> And a white splash of acid. <break time="0.8s" /> On his forehead. <break time="0.8s" /> Yes, sir. <break time="0.8s" /> Cried Wilson in surprise. <break time="0.8s" /> And Holmes sat up in his chair. <break time="0.8s" /> With great excitement. <break time="0.8s" /> After Wilson left. <break time="0.8s" /> Holmes said that it was quite a three pipe problem. <break time="0.8s" /> And asked me not to speak to him. <break time="0.8s" /> For fifty minutes. <break time="0.8s" /> He curled up in his chair. <break time="0.8s" /> With his knees drawn up to his nose. <break time="0.8s" /> And he sat smoking in silence. <break time="0.8s" /> Like a strange bird.
